summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, COPD, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for worsening dyspnea and a syncopal episode likely due to hypoxemia. The dyspnea was attributed to acute on chronic systolic heart failure and COPD exacerbation, with fluid overload evident from a weight gain of over 3 kg. He was treated with his home diuretic torsemide, antibiotics, and steroids, leading to improved oxygenation and resolution of congestion. His kidney function, initially impaired with a creatinine of 2.1, improved to 1.6 with diuresis. The elevated troponin was deemed non-ischemic, and syncope was not linked to arrhythmia. Muscle cramps prompted discontinuation of atorvastatin. Social work addressed medication affordability, and he was discharged home with stable vital signs, back at his dry weight, and instructions to monitor weight and follow up with his PCP.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
